UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile and preferences within the EduVerse application. It does not store authentication credentials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity.

email.description: The user's email address for communication and notifications.

selectedCurriculumIds.description: References to Curricula that the user is interested in or following. (Relationship: UserProfile N:N Curriculum)

selectedCourseIds.description: References to specific Courses the user is enrolled in or following. (Relationship: UserProfile N:N Course)

Curriculum.title: Curriculum
Curriculum.description: Represents a broad educational framework, academic board, or government exam category (e.g., CBSE Board, SSC Exams).

id.description: Unique identifier for the Curriculum entity.

name.description: The name of the curriculum (e.g., 'CBSE Board', 'NIOS Board', 'SSC Exams').

description.description: A detailed description of the curriculum's scope and purpose.

type.description: The category of the curriculum (e.g., 'Academic Board', 'Government Exam').

Course.title: Course
Course.description: Represents a specific academic class level (e.g., Class 10) or an individual government exam (e.g., SSC CGL Tier 1) within a curriculum.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Course entity.

name.description: The name of the course (e.g., 'Class 10', 'SSC CGL Tier 1', 'NIOS Secondary Course').

description.description: A description of the course content and learning objectives.

curriculumId.description: Reference to the parent Curriculum this course belongs to. (Relationship: Curriculum 1:N Course)

gradeLevel.description: The academic grade level if applicable (e.g., 4, 10, 12). Null or omitted for non-academic courses.

Subject.title: Subject
Subject.description: Represents a distinct academic subject or topic area within a course (e.g., Mathematics, General Awareness).

id.description: Unique identifier for the Subject entity.

name.description: The name of the subject (e.g., 'Mathematics', 'Science', 'General Intelligence').

description.description: A description outlining the scope and content of the subject.

courseId.description: Reference to the Course this subject belongs to. (Relationship: Course 1:N Subject)

LearningMaterial.title: LearningMaterial
LearningMaterial.description: Represents individual learning resources such as videos, notes, or interactive quizzes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LearningMaterial entity.

title.description: The title of the learning material.

description.description: A brief description of the material's content or purpose.

type.description: The type of learning material (e.g., 'Video', 'PDF Notes', 'Interactive Quiz', 'Audio Lecture').

contentUrl.description: The URL to access the learning material (e.g., video link, PDF download link).

subjectId.description: Reference to the Subject this material is part of. (Relationship: Subject 1:N LearningMaterial)

durationMinutes.description: The estimated duration of the material in minutes (e.g., for videos or audio lectures).

Exam.title: Exam
Exam.description: Represents a specific test, assessment, or mock exam within a subject or course.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Exam entity.

title.description: The title of the exam (e.g., 'Class 10 Math Midterm', 'SSC CGL Mock Test 1').

description.description: A description of the exam, including topics covered and instructions.

subjectId.description: Reference to the Subject this exam primarily assesses. (Relationship: Subject 1:N Exam)

durationMinutes.description: The allotted time for completing the exam in minutes.

totalMarks.description: The maximum possible marks or score for this exam.

Question.title: Question
Question.description: Represents an individual question that can be part of an exam, quiz, or a standalone practice item.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Question entity.

text.description: The actual text content of the question.

options.description: An array of possible answer choices for multiple-choice questions.

correctAnswer.description: The correct answer to the question. For multiple choice, this would typically be the text of the correct option.

explanation.description: An explanation or solution for the correct answer.

subjectId.description: Reference to the Subject this question pertains to. (Relationship: Subject 1:N Question)

examId.description: Optional reference to the Exam this question is part of. (Relationship: Exam 1:N Question)

StudyPlan.title: StudyPlan
StudyPlan.description: Represents a personalized study plan generated for a user, combining various courses, subjects, and materials.

id.description: Unique identifier for the StudyPlan entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who owns this study plan. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N StudyPlan)

title.description: A user-friendly title for the study plan (e.g., 'My Class 10 CBSE Math Plan').

description.description: A detailed description of the study plan's focus, goals, and content.

startDate.description: The date when the study plan is intended to start.

endDate.description: The date when the study plan is intended to end.

status.description: The current status of the study plan (e.g., 'Active', 'Completed', 'Draft', 'Archived').

recommendedCourseIds.description: References to Courses included or recommended in this study plan. (Relationship: StudyPlan N:N Course)

recommendedSubjectIds.description: References to Subjects included or recommended in this study plan. (Relationship: StudyPlan N:N Subject)

recommendedMaterialIds.description: References to LearningMaterials recommended for this study plan. (Relationship: StudyPlan N:N LearningMaterial)

UserProgress.title: UserProgress
UserProgress.description: Tracks a user's progress and performance across specific courses, subjects, learning materials, or exams.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProgress entity.

userId.description: Reference to the UserProfile this progress record belongs to. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N UserProgress)

entityType.description: The type of entity whose progress is being tracked (e.g., 'Course', 'Subject', 'LearningMaterial', 'Exam', 'Question').

entityId.description: The ID of the specific entity (Course, Subject, LearningMaterial, Exam, Question) being tracked.

progressPercentage.description: The percentage of completion for the tracked entity (0-100).

lastAccessedDate.description: The timestamp of the last user interaction or update for this entity.

isCompleted.description: A boolean indicating if the user has completed this specific entity.

score.description: The score achieved by the user for the entity, if applicable (e.g., for an exam or quiz).

definition.description: Stores a user's profile information. Access is restricted to the authenticated user whose ID matches the document ID. This path ensures path-based ownership and authorization independence.

A collection to store UserProfile documents for users designated as administrators. This enables role-based access control, checking for the existence of a document at `/admins/$(request.auth.uid)` to grant administrative privileges. Only an authenticated user can read if they exist in this collection.

Stores broad educational frameworks like CBSE, NIOS, or government exam categories. These documents are publicly readable by any authenticated user but require administrative privileges for write operations. No authorization dependence on parent documents.

Stores specific academic classes or individual government exams belonging to a curriculum. The `curriculumId` is denormalized implicitly by the path and explicitly in the document's `curriculumId` field. Publicly readable by authenticated users, admin-writable. Does not rely on parent document data for authorization.

Stores distinct academic subjects or topic areas within a course. The `courseId` is denormalized implicitly by the path and explicitly in the document's `courseId` field. Publicly readable by authenticated users, admin-writable. Does not rely on parent document data for authorization.

Stores individual learning resources (videos, notes, quizzes) for a subject. The `subjectId` is denormalized implicitly by the path and explicitly in the document's `subjectId` field. Publicly readable by authenticated users, admin-writable. Does not rely on parent document data for authorization.

Stores specific tests or assessments for a subject. The `subjectId` is denormalized implicitly by the path and explicitly in the document's `subjectId` field. Publicly readable by authenticated users, admin-writable. Does not rely on parent document data for authorization.

Stores individual questions, part of a subject and potentially an exam. The `subjectId` is denormalized implicitly by the path and explicitly in the document's `subjectId` field. Publicly readable by authenticated users, admin-writable. Does not rely on parent document data for authorization.
Stores personalized study plans for a user. Includes denormalized 'userId' in the path and document for authorization independence. Only the owning user can read/write their study plans.

Tracks a user's progress across courses, subjects, and materials. Includes denormalized 'userId' in the path and document for authorization independence. Only the owning user can read/write their progress records.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure for EduVerse prioritizes a clear separation between public, globally accessible educational content and private, user-specific data, adhering to all core design principles. This approach facilitates simple, robust, and easily debuggable security rules.

**Authorization Independence:**
1.  **User-Specific Data:** For entities like `UserProfile`, `StudyPlan`, and `UserProgress`, authorization independence is achieved by embedding the `userId` directly into the document path (e.g., `/users/{userId}/studyPlans/{studyPlanId}`). Furthermore, the `userId` is explicitly stored as a field within each `StudyPlan` and `UserProgress` document. This allows security rules to evaluate ownership simply by comparing `request.auth.uid` with the `userId` wildcard in the path and/or the `userId` field in the document, completely eliminating the need for expensive and complex `get()` calls to parent documents for authorization purposes. This ensures atomic creation and updates.
2.  **Public Educational Content:** For global entities such as `Curriculum`, `Course`, `Subject`, `LearningMaterial`, `Exam`, and `Question`, read access is designed to be broad (e.g., `allow read: if request.auth.uid != null;`). Write access for these public collections is restricted to administrators, whose roles are managed via a separate, flat collection (`/admins/{uid}`). This design ensures that authorization for public content does not depend on attributes of parent documents within the content hierarchy, thus maintaining authorization independence.

**Support for Query-Aware Permissions (QAPs):**
1.  **User-Specific Data:** By nesting `StudyPlan` and `UserProgress` under a user's specific path (`/users/{userId}/...`), listing operations become inherently secure. A user can only query and retrieve their own study plans or progress records. The security rules will automatically enforce this filtering based on `request.auth.uid` matching the `{userId}` in the path, without relying on client-side filtering or database-level rule-based filtering on document fields. This makes `list` operations efficient and secure.
2.  **Public Educational Content:** For collections like `/curricula`, `/courses`, `/subjects`, etc., read rules grant access to all authenticated users. This means users can directly list documents in these collections, allowing clients to perform queries and filtering (e.g., 'get all courses for curriculum X'). The rules enforce *who can access* the data, not *what data they can see* based on complex internal logic, thus supporting QAPs where the client requests a subset of permitted data.

**Structural Segregation and Consistency:**
*   User profiles, study plans, and progress tracking are isolated under `/users/{userId}/` for strict, path-based ownership.
*   Global educational content forms a logical hierarchy `/curricula/{curriculumId}/courses/{courseId}/...`, which is publicly readable but admin-writable. This ensures homogeneous security postures within each collection.
*   Admin roles are managed in a flat `/admins/{uid}` collection for efficient role-based access control without custom claims.
